text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Bulgaria's bread wheat supplies will end in the next 15-20 days and the country will need urgent imports to prevent a total grain crisis, Agriculture minister Roumen Hristov said.
-- Bulgaria's caretaker cabinet raised petrol prices by 176-178 percent and diesel price by 156 percent from today in a bid to update the prices with the latest slump of the lev. @
-- Bulgaria's Transport ministry said it would raise railway passenger fares and cargo tarriffs by 50 percent from March 1.
-- Private Bulgarian Trade and Industrial Bank shareholders decided to raise the bank's capital to 10 billion levs from 800 million levs.
-- The caretaker cabinet adopted a declaration stating a desire for a full NATO membership. @
-- Bulgaria's prime minister Stefan Sofianski discussed the priorities of the interim government with foreign diplomats in Sofia.
-- A World Bank mission is expected to arrive on Friday in Bulgaria to discuss possible bank's support for the structural reform with Bulgaria's president Petar Stoyanov.

-- An International Monetary Fund mission headed by Anne McGuirk is expected to arrive in Bulgaria on February 24 to hold talks on the introduction of a currency board system with the caretaker cabinet. @
-- Bulgaria's interim cabinet said it had reshuffled the state gas supplier Bulgargas' board of directors.

-- Bulgaria's Interior minister Bogomil Bonev said ex-ministers from the previous cabinet of Zhan Videnov were banned from leaving the country for one month because of an ongoing investigation by the Chief Prosecutor's office into their responsibility for the economic crisis in the country.

-- Bulgaria's president Petar Stoyanov is expected to veto by the end of the week the ammendments to the Electoral Law which lowered the barrier for political parties to enter parliament to three percent from four percent of the vote, the newspaper said, quoting sources from the presidency.
Bulgaria's parliament approved the ammendments by the votes of the Socialist majority at its last session before it was dissolved. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
